title: Kingdom of Hejaz
capsule: The Kingdom of Hejaz was proclaimed by Sharif Hussein bin Ali of Mecca on 2 November 1916 following the Arab Revolt against Ottoman rule, the first Arab state to gain international recognition in the modern era. Encompassing the Red Sea coastal corridor from Aqaba to Asir with the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, it was admitted to the League of Nations in 1920. Hussein's ambitions to lead a unified Arab state alienated rival Arab leaders and his British sponsors; in 1924–1926 Ibn Saud's Ikhwan forces conquered Mecca, Medina, and Jeddah, and Ibn Saud proclaimed himself King of the Hejaz and Sultan of Nejd in January 1926, absorbing the kingdom into what became Saudi Arabia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well documented from British mandate maps and League of Nations records; the western Red Sea coast frontier with Yemen was disputed and poorly delimited.
